basis: Electoral Commission estimate on election night, including 96,947 overseas and dictation votes
if_wrong: More specials amplify every swing; fewer dampen them

basis: The Commission expected about 55,000 specials disallowed this year (about five times usual), mostly people not enrolled, plus normal disallowances
if_wrong: Disallowed votes probably lean further left than average, so this is slightly generous to the left

basis: Election-day enrolment ended, but 18-24 enrolment rose from 62.16% to 74.2% between 30 Sep and 29 Oct: late enrolment moved earlier rather than disappearing
if_wrong: At 70% the coalition governs alone 59% of the time; at 100%, 43%
Overseas votes are the most Green-leaning and least NZ First-leaning group

basis: No rule change affected overseas voting
if_wrong: Mainly moves Green and NZ First final shares

basis: Each run draws one year's party-by-category pattern. 2008-2011 excluded as National landslide years; including them lowers Opportunity's chance to 42%
if_wrong: The single biggest driver: 2017/2020-style specials favour Labour, 2014/2023-style favour the coalition

value: 2023 special:ordinary ratio of the seat (or predecessor), scaled to the 2026 total, ±12%
basis: Seat-level special volumes are fairly stable; new 2025 boundaries mapped to the closest predecessor
if_wrong: Gives about 4,800 for Hamilton East; the candidate's figure of 8,000 is shown as a scenario

basis: Seat deviations correlate 0.62-0.83 between elections; using 2008-2023 instead changes almost nothing
if_wrong: Wairarapa's specials lean less to Labour than average, Mt Roskill's more

basis: Residual after seat lean; historical seat spread about 5 pts
if_wrong: Higher noise makes each flip closer to a coin toss

value: Actual 2026 fields; party-to-candidate flows from the 2023 split-vote statistics, calibrated to each seat's 2026 ordinary votes
basis: Where a party has no candidate, its voters' electorate votes go where split-vote data shows they go (e.g. Green voters mostly to Labour)
if_wrong: Mainly Hamilton East (no Green or ACT candidate): without this adjustment the coalition governs alone 2.3 points more often

value: Te Pāti Māori v Labour: template year's Māori-seat swing; v Green: that plus the Labour v Green lean
basis: Te Pāti Māori gained 1.5-13 pts on specials against Labour from 2014 to 2023; no history against Greens
if_wrong: Te Tai Tokerau is the least certain seat estimate

basis: Allows for party-specific shifts not seen in the template year
if_wrong: Mainly affects Opportunity's 8th seat and NZ First's 12th

value: Sainte-Laguë, 120 seats, 5% threshold or one electorate, overhang kept
basis: Electoral Act rules; reproduces the preliminary 131-seat projection exactly
